irishAmerican: Five Points, New York, to Irish parents
Saint Denis, to Irish dock hands
northern: Bavaria - came over as a boy

boyhood.Text: Raised on a hardscrabble farm outside {home}
His father drank and used his fists
Her father drank, and beat whoever was nearest
Orphaned young - an uncle worked him like a mule
Raised in the church by a God-fearing mother
Ran wild with the older boys in {home}
Went hungry most winters
A sickly boy, bullied by his brothers
A sickly girl the other children made fun of
Could shoot a rabbit at fifty paces before he could read
A schoolmarm beat his letters into him - he reads better than most
Grew up on stories of the Famine and the landlords
Watched Union troops burn his family's barn
Son of a Union veteran who never spoke of the war
Daughter of a Union veteran who never spoke of the war
Lost his mother when he was small
Born into money - and never let anyone forget it
His family lost everything in a fire
Followed the herds with his family across the northern plains
Rode before he could walk far
Learned to hunt elk in the Grizzlies from his uncle
Grew up hungry, the herds thinning every year
Lost his father to the soldiers when he was a boy
Sat with the old men by the fire for their stories every night
Was sent east to a government school - and ran away home

youth.Text: Left home young and never wrote back
Rode drag on a cattle drive into Valentine's stockyards
Won his first knife fight before he was twenty
Ran from his first real fight - he's never lived it down
Apprenticed to a blacksmith in {home}
Lost the girl he loved to a richer man
Caught stealing chickens; the beating taught him nothing
Ran with a street gang in the Five Points
Lied about his age to join up
Grew up on his grandfather's tales of the Lost Cause
Won his first stake at faro on a Saint Denis riverboat
Went down the mine at fourteen
Fell in with a travelling medicine show
Broke his first wild horse at fifteen
Went hungry the winter the government's rations never came
Traded furs at a post on the Dakota River
Saw a friend shot by soldiers
Fasted alone in the mountains to find his path
Ran from his first fight with soldiers, and has never forgiven himself
Kept house for her father and brothers after her mother died
Learned to shoot from her father - better than any of her brothers
Ran off with a travelling theatre company at seventeen
Went to work in a Saint Denis textile mill at thirteen
Taught herself to read from a stolen Bible
Turned down a rich man's proposal - her family never forgave her

work.Text: Worked the Annesburg coal mine, year after year
Lived through a cave-in that buried six men
Sharecropped land he'd never own
Lost a whole harvest to drought
Built a small spread outside {home}
Shot a rustler off his land
Drove herds into Valentine for the Heartlands outfits
Laid track for Cornwall's railroad, for pennies
Lost two fingers coupling cars
Hauled crates on the Saint Denis docks under Bronte's men
Fished the Lannahechee for a living
Felled timber in the Roanoke Ridge logging camps
Trapped beaver and fox up in the Grizzlies
Mauled by a bear - he still carries the marks
Ran card games on the Saint Denis riverboats
Owes money to the wrong people in Saint Denis
Made his money in Lemoyne cotton
Lost a fortune at the card tables and won half of it back
Preached hellfire at tent revivals across the territories
Learned his medicine sawing off legs in field hospitals
Studied medicine back East; the frontier wasn't what he pictured
Kept a dry goods store in {home}
Clerked at the bank in {town}
Lost his trade to the bottle
Rode the boxcars from Blackwater to Annesburg and back
Dug ditches and hauled stone wherever there was pay
Rode with a crew of road agents down in New Austin
Drifted from town to town, never more than a season
Kept the forge in {home} and shod half the horses in the county
Took over the smithy when the old smith's hands gave out
Mended wagon wheels and plough shares for every farm around {home}
Learned the forge at her father's side - she could shoe a horse before she could sew
Worked the hammer in {home} until the men who laughed at her brought her their horses
Cut suits for the gentlemen of Saint Denis in a shop off the avenue
Mended coats and trousers in {home} for whoever could pay
Studied at the Woman's Medical College in Philadelphia, then came west where a doctor is a doctor
Took in sewing in {home} to keep a roof over her head
Sewed gowns for the society ladies of Saint Denis in a shop off the avenue
Washed the miners' clothes in Annesburg for a nickel a load
Scrubbed sheets in a hotel laundry in {town} from dawn to dark
Taught the one-room schoolhouse outside {home}
Came west from back East to teach school, and stayed
Kept the general store in {town}, and kept the books better than the men
Ran the family store in {home} after the old man's heart gave out
Cooked at a boarding house in {town} for the railroad men
Cooked for a cattle outfit on the trail up from Texas
Fed the loggers in the Roanoke Ridge camps out of one iron pot
Went into service in a big house in Saint Denis at thirteen
Was let go without a reference for a broken vase she never touched
Kept a boarding house in {town} - drummers, drifters and railroad men
Trimmed hats for the ladies of {town}, feathers and all
Worked the telegraph key at the {town} station - he hears everything first
Nursed fever patients at the Saint Denis hospital
Delivered half the babies born in {home}
Took her vows at the convent in Saint Denis
Runs the soup line for the poor of Saint Denis
Followed her husband's ministry from one tent revival to the next
Married into Lemoyne cotton money
Raised money for the Saint Denis orphans' home at her own charity balls
Marched for the vote with the suffragists in Saint Denis
Danced for drinks at a Valentine saloon
Worked upstairs at a saloon in {town}, and saved every coin she could hide
Sang on the stage of a Saint Denis theatre
Toured the river towns with a travelling show
Proved up a homestead claim near {home} with her own two hands
Sold eggs and butter in {town} on market days
Worked her husband's land from first light, then cooked for the hands
Lost a whole harvest to drought, and planted again
Sold oysters and pralines at the Saint Denis market
Sold fish off the dock at Lagras before dawn
Came west by train to start over where nobody knew her name
Rode the line from Saint Denis to Blackwater to see her sister

crime.Text: Did {n} years in Sisika Penitentiary for robbery
Shot a man dead over cards in Van Horn
crime.MirrorTitle: A card game in Van Horn ends in a killing

crime.Text: Broke out of the Strawberry jail
His face is on an old wanted poster in New Austin
Ran moonshine through the bayou for a bootlegger
Got away with a payroll - and drank the lot
Held up a stagecoach on the road outside Strawberry

gang.Text: Swore himself to Colm after the Van der Linde feud cost him a friend
Owes his life to Colm O'Driscoll - and Colm never lets him forget it
Kept watch through a winter up at Six Point Cabin
Fences stolen horses in Valentine for the gang
Burned out a carpetbagger's store in Rhodes
Guards moonshine stills in Bluewater Marsh
Swears he'll never salute the Union flag
Posted to Fort Wallace under Colonel Favours
Rode with the cavalry on the plains campaigns
Disciplined for drinking on watch
Escorted a Cornwall payroll through Roanoke Ridge
Saw his sergeant shot by Raiders near Rhodes
Lost his land to the bank and blamed everyone but himself
Wears the hood because his father did
Was a cowhand on a Hennigan's Stead ranch until the owner cheated him of a season's pay
Can change a brand with a running iron faster than any man on the plains
Drove cattle up the trail from Texas and never went back
Rode with the rustlers who ran off the MacFarlane herd
Lost his own small herd to a hard winter, and took other men's after
Followed his older brother into the Laramie boys
Was nearly hanged by a cattlemen's posse in the Great Plains
Rode with bandits on both sides of the river since he was fifteen
Left Nuevo Paraiso one step ahead of the rurales
Robbed his first train near Rio Bravo
Fought in the troubles across the border before the Del Lobos took him in
Smuggles guns across the river for the jefe
Swore himself to the jefe after the jefe saved his life in Gaptooth Ridge
His face is on wanted posters in Armadillo and in Chuparosa both
Lost his farm across the river to a rich man's lawyers
Was born on a houseboat in Bayou Nwa and has never slept on dry land
Was taken in by the Night Folk as a boy, after the fever took his family
Stopped going to church in Saint Denis the year the lanterns first came
Swore himself to the elder in the dark, and has never seen his face
Lost a brother to the Lemoyne Raiders on the bayou road
Knows every channel from Lagras to Shady Belle by the sound of the water
Left a warning in the cypress that Saint Denis still talks about
Hasn't spoken a full sentence since the night of the big flood
Rides with the young men who are done waiting on the Army's promises
Keeps watch on Fort Wallace from the ridges above it
Took back horses from the Army's corrals
Listens to Rains Fall, though his heart wants to fight
Hunts for the families when the rations run short
Followed the oil men's surveyors across Wapiti land

adult.Text: Found God at a tent revival after a bad year
Stopped going to church after his mother's funeral
Won a shooting contest at a county fair
Took a bullet in a saloon brawl in {town}
Lost his savings to a crooked card sharp
Pulled a drowning boy out of the river
Lost a brother to the fever
Buried his best friend after a gunfight
Keeps to the old ways, whatever the missionaries say
Stopped praying the winter his mother died
Lost a brother to the coughing sickness
Won a horse race against riders from three bands
Was jailed in Valentine for a fight he didn't start
Buried a friend the soldiers killed
Taught his nephews to track the way his uncle taught him
Snakebit out in the scrub - nearly died
Started drinking hard and never stopped
Beat a bigger man bare-knuckle in {town}
Backed down from a duel in Armadillo
Saves every cent he makes
Sends money home to his mother every month
Shot his own horse when it broke a leg, and wept
Sat out a blizzard alone in the Grizzlies for nine days
Nursed half of {town} through a diphtheria winter
Joined the temperance women and took an axe to a saloon's bottles
Keeps a pistol in her apron since a man broke into her kitchen
Ran the house on what her husband didn't drink away
Won the pie contest at the {town} fair three years running
Lost a baby to the fever, and never speaks of it
Waited three years for a sweetheart who never came back from the gold fields
